# Dr. Riad Al Chami

> Assistant Professor of Marketing, College of Business Administration, American University in the Emirates, Dubai, UAE. ORCID https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6254-8459. Also published as Riad AlChami, Riad Alchami, Riad El Chami, Riad Al-Chami.

Riad Al Chami is an Assistant Professor of Marketing at the College of Business Administration, American University in the Emirates (AUE), Dubai, where he also directs the MBA program. His research examines how organizations institutionalize corporate social responsibility, how green communication can turn into greenwashing or greenbleaching, how sustainability shapes supply chains and airline marketing, and how artificial intelligence and immersive technologies change brand trust, engagement and strategic communication. His work appears in Business Strategy and the Environment, Corporate Communications: An International Journal, Journal of Global Marketing, Administrative Sciences and Innovative Marketing, and in books from Springer Nature and IGI Global.

Research areas: Corporate Social Responsibility; Green Communication; Sustainable Supply Chain Management; Consumer Behavior; AI in Marketing.

## Publications

- [Immersive Augmented Reality and Global Brand Engagement: Satisfaction Mechanisms in International Marketing Environments](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/immersive-augmented-reality-global-brand-engagement.html): Riad Al Chami, Sam El Nemar, Demetris Vrontis (2026), Journal of Global Marketing. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1080/08911762.2026.2745960. Using survey data from COP28 visitors, this study shows that immersive augmented reality brand experiences raise global customer engagement, and that customer satisfaction is the mechanism that carries the effect.
- [The Influence of Perceived Value Factors on Electric Vehicle Purchasing Intention: The Moderating Effect of the Lebanese Economic Crisis](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/ev-purchase-intention-lebanese-economic-crisis.html): Mahmoud Edelby, Riad Alchami, Ghalia Nassreddine, Mazen Massoud (2026), Innovative Marketing. DOI: https://doi.org/10.21511/im.22(1).2026.23. A study of 124 potential car buyers in Lebanon shows that electric vehicle purchase intention is driven mainly by technical performance and economics, and that the economic crisis changes how much each factor matters.
- [Supply Chain Sustainability Performance in the Manufacturing Sector of a Developing Economy](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/supply-chain-sustainability-performance-manufacturing.html): Mohammad A. K. Alsmairat, Riad Al-Chami, Jose Arturo Garza-Reyes, Daniel Luiz de Mattos Nascimento (2026), Business Strategy and the Environment. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1002/bse.70169. A survey of 390 operations managers in five Middle Eastern countries shows what actually drives sustainable supply chain performance in manufacturing, and finds that regulation matters less than competition, internal resources and customer demand.
- [From Talk to Trust: Cultural Dynamics of AI-Driven Social Responsibility in Negotiations for Strategic Communication](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/from-talk-to-trust-ai-driven-social-responsibility.html): Riad Al Chami (2025), International Communication of Chinese Culture. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s40636-025-00331-4. Through cases of Patagonia, Ben & Jerry's, Unilever and H&M, this study shows how socially responsible, AI-supported negotiation and transparent communication build consumer trust and loyalty, and how superficial CSR backfires as greenwashing.
- [Challenging Patriarchy: The Transformation of Women's Roles Under Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/challenging-patriarchy-saudi-vision-2030.html): Riad Al Chami, Moustafa Haj Youssef (2025), Impact of Patriarchy and Gender Stereotypes on Working Women: Exploring Its Past, Present and Future. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-74406-8_7. This chapter examines how Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 legal and educational reforms are changing women's roles at work and in society, and what is still needed to reach real gender parity.
- [From Greenwashing to Greenbleaching: Green Communication and Mitigating Moral Outrage in the Context of Revisited Situational Crisis Communication Theory](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/from-greenwashing-to-greenbleaching.html): Marko Selaković, Nikolina Ljepava, Noushin Bagheri, Riad Al Chami (2025), Corporate Communications: An International Journal. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1108/CCIJ-01-2024-0011. This study introduces greenbleaching: the exaggerated or fabricated use of green communication to deflect a crisis that has nothing to do with environmental, social or governance issues. It draws on 66 crisis cases analysed through Situational Crisis Communication Theory.
- [Integrating Sustainability in Aviation: A Comprehensive Analysis of Emirates Airlines' Strategies in Global Marketing and Consumer Dynamics](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/integrating-sustainability-in-aviation-emirates-airlines.html): Riad Al Chami (2025), Navigating Business Through Essential Sustainable Strategies. DOI: https://doi.org/10.4018/979-8-3693-5360-8.ch006. Combining Emirates Group employee views with corporate data, this chapter shows how sustainability strategy supports Emirates Airlines' global market position and customer loyalty.
- [Managing UAE Supply Chain Carbon Footprint: Sustainability and Climate Change Mitigation Strategies](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/managing-uae-supply-chain-carbon-footprint.html): Riad Al Chami (2023), Polish Journal of Management Studies. DOI: https://doi.org/10.17512/pjms.2023.28.1.01. A survey of 90 UAE supply chain workers examines carbon footprint awareness and finds that younger, more educated workers are more engaged, which points to education as a lever for decarbonising supply chains.
- [The Institutionalization of Implicit and Explicit CSR in a Developing Country Context: The Case of Lebanon](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/institutionalization-implicit-explicit-csr-lebanon.html): Samer Kobrossy, Robert Karaszewski, Riad AlChami (2022), Administrative Sciences. DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/admsci12040142. A qualitative study of Lebanese organizations explains which institutional pressures drive explicit (formal, communicated) versus implicit (embedded, norm-based) corporate social responsibility in a developing country.
- [Organizational Culture and Leadership Practices Impact on the Satisfaction of the Customer](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/organizational-culture-leadership-customer-satisfaction.html): Riad El Chami (2022), Organizational Culture in the Middle East: A Lebanese Perspective. A survey of 200 senior managers in international companies in Lebanon and Dubai links employee motivation, employee involvement, leadership practices and organizational vision to customer satisfaction.
- [Online Shopping Consumer Behavior: Why Are We Afraid to Purchase Online? Case Study Lebanon](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/online-shopping-consumer-behavior-lebanon.html): Riad El Chami (2018), International Journal of Management and Commerce Innovations. This study explains why Lebanese consumers hesitate to buy online, pointing to low trust in e-commerce sites, poor website usability and high perceived risk.
- [Significance of Marketing in School](https://riadalchami-cloud.github.io/significance-of-marketing-in-school.html): Riad El Chami, Fadel Yakhne (2018), International Journal of Management and Commerce Innovations. Based on interviews with admissions heads in Tripoli, Lebanon, this study identifies what drives parents' school choice and turns it into a marketing strategy for schools.
